Modal Contact as a Dynamic Two-Way Constraint

Promote the support's modal amplitude q into a dynamic degree of freedom solved jointly with the bodies — so contact loads the modes and the ringing modes push the bodies back. Two-way and passive by construction; no separate velocity band, no energy governor.

DCR follow-up · unified dynamic constraint (Approach B) · two native GPU-resident solvers (AVBD · XPBD), no coupler · backward-Euler or implicit-midpoint over (z, q)

The energy loop: cubes ride the ringing support, both damp to rest

dynamic support surface yrest+Uy·q — the full q (sag + ring), one curve static-sag equilibrium — where it settles dropped impactor — rings the support; bystanders get kicked through it

What changed: from a two-band split to one dynamic constraint

The earlier design split the support's deformation: the static sag qs went into the contact constraint, while the fast ring q̇d was evolved separately and injected as a capped, one-way velocity impulse. That seam is exactly why energy only flowed rigid → support and never looped back.

The fix is to stop splitting. Carry the full, dynamic modal state q as a second-order DOF — with its own inertia Mq, stiffness Kq, damping Dq — inside the same contact solve as the bodies. One backward-Euler step minimizes a single incremental potential over (z, q). The two-way loop is then structural, not injected: the contact force that lifts a cube is the very reaction that loads the mode, and the mode's inertia pushes back.

Deleted along the way: qs/qd split · drift-fix · separate IIR resonator for in-contact ring · velocity band · η / energy reservoir governor · high-pass / cooldown. The static sag is no longer special — it is just the equilibrium of the dynamic q under gravity.

Where it stands now: two native solvers, no coupler, GPU-resident this branch

The dynamic (z, q) step above is no longer prototyped through an external "coupler." It is implemented natively inside two genuinely independent solvers — each carries q (and any deformable-cargo elastic block a) as its own DOF in its own formulation, over a single shared constraint interface and the same SAT box-box manifold; only the per-constraint projection differs. The coupler architecture was deleted. numpy stays the obviously-correct parity reference; both device paths are validated against it.

A unified viser drives scene × solver × material × device live (scenes: shelf · ledge · dinner · truck · cargo). A robustness benchmark sweeps relax × budget × scene, flagging any config that injects energy, kills the two-way loop, blows up, or detunes the ring off its Euler–Bernoulli frequency.

The two kinds of unknowns

z — the rigid bodies' state: position + orientation (and velocity v = [vlin; ω]). Ordinary rigid DOFs, one block of 6 per body.

q — the modal amplitudes. The solve carries the augmented vector Q = [qsupport; ab0; ab1; …] — the support's field and each cargo cube's elastic modes, block-diagonal (mass-normalized, so Mq=I, Kq=diag(ω²)). A dynamic DOF with state (Q, Q̇) — not a passive output.

Both are advanced by the same implicit step. The contact is the only thing that couples them.

Contact as a constraint on (z, Q) one gap · two special cases

Every contact reads the deformed contact point of both participants — the rigid pose plus the modal flex Φ·a:

Cj(z,Q) = n̂·(pA − pB), pX = xX + RX( r̄X + ΦXaX ) = Crigid + ( ĜA·aA − ĜB·aB ) # ĜX = n̂ᵀRXΦX

Gradients: ∂C/∂z = Jx = [n̂; r×n̂];  ∂C/∂aA = +ĜA,  ∂C/∂aB = −ĜB. The single objects coupling body↔mode are ĜA, ĜB.

Two special cases of the same gap. support row: B is the world-fixed slab (no rigid DOF), n̂=ŷ, ĜA→Uy ⇒ C = cornery − (yrest + Uy·q).  box-box row: both are cargo cubes ⇒ a stacked cube feels the ring of the cube under it (§N2, both a-blocks loaded). The rigid ride bakes the same flex into the primal gap so z is driven too, not just a.

Unilateral, compressive-only: fj = clamp(ρ Cj + λj, −∞, 0).

One variational step over (z, q) the formulation

Each substep minimizes a single incremental potential (backward Euler / AVBD augmented-Lagrangian). The only structural change from the static coupler is the highlighted modal-inertia term — that one term is what gives q a life of its own:

E(z,q) = Σi 1⁄(2h²)‖zi − z̃i‖²Mi # rigid inertia + 1⁄(2h²)‖q − q̃‖²Mq # modal inertia ◀ NEW + ½ qᵀKqq # modal stiffness + Σj ΦAL( gj(z,q) ) # contact — sees the FULL q

Inertial predictors (the modal one carries the ring's history q̇n — not zeroed, which is the whole point):

z̃i = zin + h vin + h² Mi−1 fiext q̃ = qn + h q̇n + h² Mq−1 fqgrav # fqgrav = Uᵀfgrav → gives the static sag at equilibrium

The Newton / Schur block — only Hq gains two terms

Stationarity ∇E = 0 gives the same monolithic system you already assemble; the cross-block −ρ JxUyᵀ is unchanged. The static Hq=Kq+Σk UyUyᵀ simply gains an inertia and a damping term:

[ Hx,i −ρ Jx,i Uy,jᵀ ] [Δzi] [ −gx,i ] [ ] [ ] = [ ] [ −ρ Uy,j Jx,iᵀ Hq ] [Δq ] [ −gq ] Hq = 1⁄h²·Mq + 1⁄h·Dq + Kq + Σj kj Uy,jUy,jᵀ gq = 1⁄h²·Mq(q−q̃) + 1⁄h·Dq(q−qn) + Kqq − Σj Uy,j fj

After the step: q̇n+1 = (qn+1 − qn)/h. The new terms are diagonal additions.

How it is actually solved. Rather than factor the full monolithic matrix, both solvers use block coordinate descent: the colored primal advances z, then an engaged-gated Hq block advances q — and only compressive support corners (fj < 0) enter Hq/gq, so a separated corner cannot stiffen the mode. The explicit cross-term Schur (assemble −ρ JxUyᵀ and eliminate Δz) was tried and rejected: without the Δz back-substitution it injects energy, and the cross-only form softens Hq so the livelier ring topples resting stacks. XPBD condenses the same rows with a Woodbury block solve; AVBD gathers them into the primal Hq.

Body↔body (§N2). The very same block spans two cargo cubes: a box-box row contributes +ĜA to cube A's a-block and −ĜB to cube B's, loaded by one shared fj — the support row above is the degenerate case (participant B world-fixed, ĜA→Uy). Engaged-gating + relax carry over unchanged; the −Uy column simply becomes ±Ĝ on both sides.

Why it is two-way & momentum-conserving

There is one multiplier fj per contact. It enters the two gradients with opposite signs through the same scalar:

rigid: gx += +Jx,j fj ⌉ one fj, modal: gq += −Uy,j fj ⌋ opposite signs

That is Newton's third law. The force lifting the cube is exactly the reaction loading the mode — resolved to convergence each step. Because q now has inertia, when the mode springs back it raises the anchor and pushes the cube. The loop is built in.

Body↔body: for a box-box row the same fj loads +ĜA on cube A's modes and −ĜB on cube B's — the third law now on the augmented Q. Slab⇄cube is the special case where B is the world-fixed slab.

Passive for free no governor

Backward Euler on this potential is unconditionally dissipative: total mechanical energy is monotone non-increasing every step,

Ė = −q̇ᵀDqq̇ − Σ viᵀCivi ≤ 0

so the run can only converge to argmin E = the static sag. The old ΔEmodal ≤ η·ΔErigid loss reservoir is unnecessary — it was needed only because the split injected energy one-way. A momentum-conserving shared multiplier never injects.

Backward Euler is the default (the parity reference). When the ring should decay at the physical rate rather than BE's numerical one, an energy-conserving implicit-midpoint modal step is available — still co-solved inside the same constraint, so still passive. See the boundary note below.

Honest boundary of the claim read before believing

Numerical damping. Plain backward Euler removes energy even with Dq=0, so under BE the ring decay you see is physical damping plus integrator damping. That is why the branch now also carries an energy-conserving implicit-midpoint modal step (Hq = 2Mq/h² + Dq/h + ½Kq, commit q̇n+1 = 2(qn+1−qn)/h − q̇n): A-stable, undamped it conserves modal energy, damped it decays at the physical rate. BE stays the default parity reference; midpoint is opt-in.

Timescale / fidelity. At a typical substep h ∼ 1–4 ms, modes above ∼1/(2h) are over-damped / under-resolved. Low modes (visible sag & sway, <100 Hz) are faithful; a crisp kHz ring needs finer h or a hybrid that keeps an exact-exponential resonator for airborne intervals only.

Novelty. The physics here is classical flexible-multibody coupling (floating-frame + component-mode-synthesis; equivalently the affine-body / IPC family, but with modal rather than affine reduction). What is unestablished is realizing it as constraints inside a real-time position-based / augmented-Lagrangian rigid solver (XPBD and AVBD, GPU-resident) — both are now built and cross-validated on this branch. This in-solver step is the ground truth; the cheaper, approximate, passivity-governed coupling is where the energy-bound contribution actually lives — validated against this.

Validation — the loop is real solver output, not a schematic measured

Everything above is a claim; this section is the evidence, logged from the native solvers on the shelf scene (a 6 kg impactor dropped on the reduced-modal support, with a 1 kg "book" resting nearby). Per support-contact corner we log the scalar normal force Fc — the same multiplier that lifts the body and deflects the mode (∂C/∂q = −Uy), so the two directions of the loop are literally one shared constraint. Reproduce: scripts/run_native_energy_loop_verification.py.

The loop, annotated

One shared contact multiplier carries both arrows: slab → object (the ring launches the resting book) and object → slab (each landing re-rings the slab). impactor 29 J → slab modal ring 3303 mJ → object launch 395 mJ, then modal + contact damping → rest.

Four-corner contact force + the energy loop shelf · XPBD · 16 iters × 4 substeps

Panel 1 (energies). The impactor KE (blue) charges then dumps at 250 ms; the slab modal ring (red) peaks next; the resting object's mechanical energy (green) rises after that — the ordering (slab peaks before object) proves the ring drives the object, not vice-versa. Panel 2. The book lifts 38.9 mm and goes airborne (shaded) — 5 bounces, each re-ringing the slab. Panels 3–4 (the four-corner force). A box has 8 support rows; the four load-bearing corners carry the load and the top four read ≈0. The impactor's four corners spike to 569 N at the strike (repeated spikes = rebounds); the resting book's four corners settle to ≈2.5 N each (4 × 2.5 ≈ m·g — the calibration that says the force is physically real), with transients as each ring passes.

The discriminating control: freeze the ring, the feedback dies

Re-run with the modal velocity frozen (q̇≡0): the slab can still deflect quasi-statically but cannot ring or feed energy back. Solid = two-way (q active), dashed = one-way (frozen). Left — XPBD: freezing collapses the object-KE peak by 29× (slab 3303 → 293 mJ); the launch is unambiguously slab-ring-driven. That is what "two-way" means. Right — AVBD, same config: honestly only 1.0× here — the slab still rings (1390 vs 840 mJ, so the inertial ring is real), but AVBD's conservative, dissipative block solve barely transmits it to the book; its coupling emerges only at high convergence (dinner reaches 42× at 32×8). Reported as-is, not cherry-picked.

Honest boundary. XPBD is strongly two-way at every budget but injects energy below ~16 iterations (the under-convergence blow-up — slab ring can exceed the impactor input); energy is bounded only at iters ≥ 16. AVBD stays energy-bounded in every config but is too dissipative to show a strong loop unless well-converged. The two-way coupling is real in both; the energy magnitude at low budgets is a solver artifact. Full sweep + per-corner traces for shelf/ledge/dinner × {avbd,xpbd}: docs/native_energy_loop/.

Quantitative eval — the coupler's passivity bound, measured across 106 runs follow-up B1–B7

Which method this measures. Not the native (z,q) solver above — that one is passive by construction (backward-Euler dissipativity), evidenced by the loop/control plots in this section. This benchmark measures the other path: the cheaper, approximate passivity-governed coupler (the deleted-from-this-branch injection method, mode=energy_prescribed_patch) that the boundary note calls "where the energy-bound contribution actually lives." Its guarantee is the §15 bound ΔEmodal ≤ η·ΔErigid loss (cumulative) — an explicit passive-α cap, not structural. The seven-sweep suite (scripts/benchmark/run_b1.py…run_b7.py on the benchmark-suite branch; CPU numpy reference) puts a number on it.

B1 is the discriminating experiment: the same three scenes run twice — once with the paper's forced-IIR modal stepper (Eq. 10 + Eq. 12), once with the §15-governed coupler — logging the worst per-step violation of the cumulative bound and the injected-to-budget ratio.

sceneforced-IIR baseline paper Eq. 10§15-governed this work
ledgeviolates bound by 250 J · inject/budget 1.636×10⁻¹⁴ J · ratio 0.90
shelfviolates by 678 J · inject/budget 3.030 J · ratio 0.72
truckviolates by ≈14,000 J · inject/budget 3.425×10⁻¹³ J · ratio 0.81

Reading: a ratio > 1 means the modal path injected more energy than the rigid contact lost — the forced stepper is not passive and overshoots the budget by 1.6–3.4×. The governed injection holds the bound to machine precision (violation ~10⁻¹³ J = round-off) while still delivering 72–90% of the available budget into the modes.

Robustness (B2–B7). The remaining six sweeps stress the same invariant: deformed-normal method (B2), β energy-budget fraction ∈ {0.1…1.0} (B3), transfer efficiency η ∈ {0.1…1.0} (B4), material wood vs. steel (B5), runtime (B6), timestep h ∈ {0.001…0.025} (B7). Across all 106 runs, the only configurations that violate the §15 bound are the three forced-IIR baselines above; every one of the other 103 governed runs holds to < 2×10⁻¹² J. The η sweep (B4) confirms the bound is the right knob: the injected fraction tracks the η·ΔEloss budget monotonically (ratio 0.80→0.89 as η goes 1.0→0.1) and never exceeds it.

Honest boundary of this eval read before believing — (1) The pass/fail rubric fails everywhere, including the paper baseline. It is a strict 1 mm penetration + tilt rubric on the rigid solver (PGS+Baumgarte at h=10 ms penetrates v·h≈9 mm on impact by construction; shelf books tip to 90° as their natural physics). It is orthogonal to the energy claim — the passivity result is what B1–B7 actually establish, not visual quality. (2) Not real-time: 16–96 ms/step on the CPU numpy reference (B6); the GPU-resident native path is this branch's perf story and is not what these numbers measure. (3) Scope: three primitive scenes + the dinner scene; no high-resolution FEM or SOFA ground-truth comparison yet, and no perceptual user study. (4) On the wood truck scene the residual ring needs β≤0.2 + light damping to stop visible trailing vibration (a magnitude rule on top of the passivity rule); steel does not exhibit it.

Generalization — from slab⇄cube to cube⇄cube: the modal contact network §N2 · this branch

Everything above couples a cube to the slab's ring through one shared multiplier. Nothing in that derivation needs the other side to be a slab. Aim the same constraint at a second cargo cube and a stacked cube feels the ring of the cube under it — the slab support is just the degenerate case where one participant carries no modes.

box-box gap: Cj(z,a) = n̂·(rA − rB) + n̂ᵀRAΦA·aA − n̂ᵀRBΦB·aB ≥ 0 ∂C/∂aA = +n̂ᵀRAΦA ∂C/∂aB = −n̂ᵀRBΦB one fj loads BOTH a-blocks, opposite signs # Newton's 3rd law on Q

Each cube's co-rotated modal column GX = n̂ᵀRXΦc enters the augmented q-block through the same box-box multiplier — exactly the −Uyf / +Gaf pairing the support path uses, now on both sides of the contact. The solver auto-discovers every cargo⇄cargo joint each substep (_build_net_rows); OFF, _net_rows is empty ⇒ the trajectory is bit-identical to the pre-network path.

Real solver output — a 3-high offset stack (base▸mid▸upper) beside a dropped impactor (scenes/reduced_cargo_network.py, AVBD, 12 iters × 4 substeps). Top: the impactor rings the slab q (blue), the slab rings base (green, support path), and through two box-box hops the ring climbs to mid (yellow) then upper (orange). Network OFF, mid/upper are structurally uncoupled — their modes are exactly zero (a 0-vs-nonzero discriminator). base rings higher OFF: uncoupled, it keeps all its ring energy; ON, it sheds energy up the tower (and the added contact term is backward-Euler dissipative). The rigid-ride half — now implemented, stable with friction §N2 rigid ride N3 partial

Two effects can cross a box-box contact: (1) the modal↔modal transfer — both cubes' modes ring through the shared multiplier (the robust result above) — and (2) the rigid ride — the stacked body physically riding the deforming surface beneath it. Effect (2) was deferred at the N3 stability gate; it is now wired. The box-box primal/dual gap reads the same flex the q-block already sees:

primal/dual gap: C = Crigid + (ĜA·aA − ĜB·aB) # c_rest[j], baked host-side from the live a

So the same flex now drives z as well as a — the fully-symmetric unified gap. Behind _modal_contact_ride (default OFF, requires the network on); OFF, every box-box c_rest stays 0 ⇒ bit-identical. The pre-registered N3 pump (two resonators through an on/off unilateral contact) is tamed by a per-joint compressive-engagement gate + hysteresis, an under-relax, and a capped, penetration-safe flex refreshed each q-block sweep from the live a (not frozen — the staleness that helped the first cut walk an offset stack off its base).

Real solver output. Left: the demo 3-high offset stack (μ=0.4, the shipped config) with the ride ON — every cube holds its rest height; the N3 pump does not walk it off. Middle — the payoff: the mid↔upper box-box normal force. Ride OFF the ring hammers a rigid contact, so the force chatters (±1.5 N, spiking 0→15 N); ride ON the stacked body rides the deforming surface and the chatter collapses (±0.2 N, ~7× smoother) while the mean stays pinned at the supported weight m·g — the ride removes the impact chatter without touching the force balance. Right: a controlled 2-cube stack, δy = yupper(ride ON) − (ride OFF) isolates the ride — a bounded, flex-scale rigid response (~15 µm rms, ≤ 0.2 mm total) that is exactly zero with the ride off.

box-box jointforce mean (→ weight)force ripple OFF → ONchatter ↓
base↔mid11.8 N (2 m·g = 11.77)±2.0 N → ±0.45 N4.4×
mid↔upper5.9 N (m·g = 5.89)±1.5 N → ±0.22 N6.9×

What works. Bit-identical when off; the demo stack + 2-cube stacks (aligned & offset, μ=0.4) and settled frictionless stacks stay standing; the ride is stable with friction and its clearest signature is the 3–7× drop in box-box contact-force chatter — the stacked body tracks the surface instead of impacting it. Honest limits (both pre-registered as the N3 gate): (i) a frictionless-offset stack under a hard drop transient can still tunnel — friction holds the metastable tower against the ring-induced rocking; no gate/relax/cap value fixed it. (ii) The direct rigid displacement is small (~15 µm) and noisy at 12 iterations — a genuine flex-scale effect, not a clean phase-locked ripple. So the rigid-ride is an honest partial N3 win, enabled where friction makes it safe; the clean, robust §N2 result is still the modal↔modal transfer above. See docs/network/n2.md, tests/avbd_native/test_modal_contact_ride.py (6 tests).
